# New-ZbxProxy

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a proxy.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxProxy [[-Name] <string>] [[-OperatingMode] <ZabbixProxyOperatingMode>] [-ProxyGroupId <ulong>] [-LocalAddress <string>] [-LocalPort <string>] [-Description <string>] [-AllowedAddresses <string>] [-Address <string>] [-Port <string>] [-TlsConnect <ZabbixTlsConnectMode>] [-TlsAccept <ZabbixTlsAcceptModes>] [-TlsPskIdentity <string>] [-TlsPsk <SecureString>] [-TlsIssuer <string>] [-TlsSubject <string>] [-CustomTimeouts <bool>] [-TimeoutZabbixAgent <string>] [-TimeoutSimpleCheck <string>] [-TimeoutSnmpAgent <string>] [-TimeoutExternalCheck <string>] [-TimeoutDbMonitor <string>] [-TimeoutHttpAgent <string>] [-TimeoutSshAgent <string>] [-TimeoutTelnetAgent <string>] [-TimeoutScript <string>] [-TimeoutBrowser <string>] [-HostReference <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHost>[]>] [-Apm <ZabbixProxyApmRequest>] [-TimeoutTelemetryQuery <string>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A proxy collects data for the server from the hosts assigned to it, so a remote site needs only one connection to the server. The New-ZbxProxy cmdlet sends proxy.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new proxy back with proxy.get and writes it. The server requires -Name and -OperatingMode; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create an active proxy

```powershell
New-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-01' -OperatingMode Active | Select-Object ProxyId, Name, OperatingMode
```

An active proxy connects to the server itself, so only its name is needed: it must match the proxy's Hostname= setting. The created proxy is read back and written.

### Example 2: Create a passive proxy the server polls

```powershell
New-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-02' -OperatingMode Passive -Address '10.0.0.40' -Port '10051' -Description 'DMZ collector' |
    Select-Object Name, OperatingMode, Address, Port, Description
```

A passive proxy is polled by the server at -Address/-Port (strings, as the API has them).

### Example 3: Create a proxy and hand it hosts

```powershell
New-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-01' -OperatingMode Active -AllowedAddresses '10.0.0.0/24' -Host 'web-01', 'db-01' | Out-Null
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01', 'db-01' | Select-Object TechnicalName, MonitoredBy, ProxyId
```

-Host takes host names, ids or objects: those hosts are monitored by this proxy from now on (their MonitoredBy becomes Proxy). -AllowedAddresses limits where an active proxy may connect from.

### Example 4: Create an active proxy that must use TLS with a pre-shared key

```powershell
$identity = ConvertTo-SecureString 'proxy-01-psk' -AsPlainText -Force
$psk = ConvertTo-SecureString '1f87b595725ac58dd977beef14b97461a7c1045b9a1c963065002c5473194952' -AsPlainText -Force
New-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-01' -OperatingMode Active -TlsAccept Psk -TlsPskIdentity $identity -TlsPsk $psk |
    Select-Object Name, TlsAccept
```

-TlsAccept is what the server accepts from an active proxy; the PSK and its identity are SecureStrings and are never read back.
